## Run evals from the API

The shortest useful loop — create a run with o
fast on errors)\nRUN_ID=$(curl -fsS -X POST \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs\" \\\n -H \"Auth
orization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n -d '{\n \"suiteName\": \"smoke\",\n \"

serverIds": ["'$SERVER_ID'"],
 "tests": [{
 "title": "echo works",

The decision summary composes steps 2 and 4 into on

e versioned object so every
client reads a run the same way. Four things to know before gating on it:

* **`measurementUnit` sh
ips with every count.** Under per-case grading the\n counts are case-execution *variants*, with iterations as trials inside them;
\n under a suite-wide accuracy threshold they are trials. The same suite reports\n a different total under each — 3 against 15 f

or three cases run five times —
 so a count without its unit is not a fact, and a rate is never converted
 across that line.
* **It explains the verdict; it never re-decides it.** The run's own decision is\n the authority and is carried through on `decis
ion`. The per-trial\n `diagnostics` sit underneath it — a case can pass with a failing trial in it,\n so tallying diagnostics gi
ves a different answer than the platform reached.\n* **`verdict: \"notEstablished\"` is not a failure and not `inconclusive`.** It
\n means no verdict exists at all (unfinished, stopped early, or undecidable);\n `undecided.reason` says which. `inconclusive` *
is* a decision — the validity\n phase ran and withheld a verdict.\n* **`diagnostics.complete` says whether you have the whole lis
t.** A page\n fetched with a `cursor` is never complete, and `scannedIterations` separates\n \"nothing failed\" from \"we did no

t look".

Evidence is scoped to the claim it supports: for a measured failure the span
ids, prompt indexes and reasons come fr
om the first failed stage's row alone,\nand `evidence.tracePath` is an API-relative path you can append to your base URL\nto read

the full trace.

`model` takes an id from the hosted catalog — `provider/name` form, e.g.
`anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` — and ru
ns on your organization's credits.\nProvider-native ids (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-5`) are bring-your-own-key: pass\nthe key in `model
ApiKeys`. A model the API can't execute is rejected at\ncreate time with `VALIDATION_ERROR`; `details.hostedModels` lists the vali

d
hosted ids for that provider.

Reruns are even shorter: `{ "suiteId": "..." }` reruns the suite exactly as
configured, c
onnecting the suite's saved server selection (the `202` response\nlists the resolved `servers`). Pass `serverIds` to override the
selection; a\nsuite with no saved selection requires it (`VALIDATION_ERROR` with\n`details.reason: \"NO_SAVED_SERVER_SELECTION\"`

otherwise).

### Running against a project environment

A [project environment](#endpoints) is launchable only through a suite

that has
it **attached**. Attach them first with
`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}` and an `environmentIds`
a
rray (send `null` to detach them all; `[]` is rejected — use `null`), then\npass `environmentId` on the run. It must be one of tha
t suite's attached\nenvironments; anything else is a `400` with\n`details.reason: \"ENVIRONMENT_NOT_ATTACHED\"`, raised before any

case is
authored or any server connected.

Omitting `environmentId` is meaningful, and depends on the suite:

* **no** attac
hed environments → the run uses the saved server selection, as before;\n* **exactly one** attached → that environment is used auto
matically. The `202`\n response's `environment` field says so;\n* **several** attached → `400` with `details.reason: \"ENVIRONMEN

T_REQUIRED"`,
 naming the candidates.

The environment supplies the closed server set — including the servers its
pinned plu
gin versions contribute — so `serverIds` is not required and is\n**rejected** alongside it (`400`), rather than accepted and ignor
ed: honoring\nboth would connect a different set than the run is stamped with. The same goes\nfor a `serverIds` override on an env

ironment-based suite
(`details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_SERVERS_NOT_OVERRIDABLE"`).

The run is pinned to the environment revisio
n resolved at launch: if the\nenvironment changes in between, the run is rejected with `CONFLICT` (409)\nrather than executing aga
inst a different configuration than the one whose\ntools were captured. Use\n`GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentI

d}/resolve` to see what it
will connect before launching.

When creating a new inline suite, `POST .../eval-runs` also accepts
`hosts: [{ host: \"Claude\", servers: [\"my-server\"] }]`, using the same host name or ID and optional server selection as `POST .
../eval-suites`. A single host is selected for the run automatically. With multiple attachments, use `namedHostId` to select the r
un's client. For an existing suite, update its attachments first. If `hosts` is omitted, the backend supplies the project's defaul
t client.\n\nRun reads and listings expose `client: { id, name, source, hostStyle?, modelId? }` when recorded. `id` is the named h
ost ID or `null`; `source` is `environment`, `attached_host`, `suite_default`, or `sdk`. The name is durable even if the host is d
eleted. SDK executions use `SDK harness`; `launcher.client` separately identifies the launching process. Older runs without a desc
riptor omit `client`. `modelSource: \"case\"` means the run's sole model came from its case snapshot; `client_default` and `overri

de` retain their existing meanings.

Every run records which environment it used. `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}` (and
the run list
ings) return `environment: { id, name, revision }` — read from the\nrun's immutable snapshot, not the suite's current attachments

— or `null` for a
run that used a saved server selection.

Per-organization
concurrency is capped (default **2** concurrent ru

ns); exceeding it returns
`429` with `details.reason: "CONCURRENT_RUN_LIMIT"` — wait for an active run
to finish.

If a serv
er answers `401 OAUTH_REQUIRED`, complete the OAuth flow yourself\n(the SDK's `runOAuthLogin` handles interactive, headless, and\n
client-credentials flows) and upload the token to one of the server's\n[accounts](#server-accounts). Subsequent runs inject the st

ored token, and
refresh it server-side when you stored a refresh token.
